turns.question: I'd like to hear about your coffee routine and how it's changed over time. Think back to a recent moment when you decided to try something different with your coffee—maybe a new brand, a different way of making it, or even just switching where you get it from. What was going on that made you decide to make that change?
turns.response: I switched to buying from this local roaster a few months back instead of just grabbing whatever at the grocery store. Honestly I was just tired of the coffee tasting kind of flat, and my roommate wouldn't stop talking about how much better fresh beans are. So I figured why not try it, didn't cost that much more.

turns.question: When you say it "didn't cost that much more," what difference in price would've made you hesitate about switching to the local roaster?
turns.response: Honestly, I'm not really sure. I didn't do the math on it or anything. It was just like... a couple bucks more per bag maybe? If it had been like double the price I probably would've stuck with what I was buying before, but it wasn't that extreme so it didn't feel like a big deal.

turns.question: Why was it worth paying a bit more to get that fresher taste instead of sticking with the flat coffee?
turns.response: Honestly, flat coffee just tastes kind of... off after a while. Like, you notice it immediately when you take a sip and it's been sitting there. With fresher stuff the flavor's actually there, you know? I wasn't really thinking about it as paying more — it was more like, why would I drink something that tastes worse when I'm already buying coffee anyway.

turns.question: So it sounds like freshness matters most when you're actively choosing coffee, but day-to-day you're pretty flexible—is that fair, or am I missing something?
turns.response: Yeah, that's pretty much it. Like when I'm actually at the store or ordering something, I'll pay attention to the date. But once I've got it at home I'm not like checking it every morning or anything. It's more just... if it's been sitting there for months I'll notice it tastes off, but I'm not going to throw it out.
